title: Leavenworth to Mount Rainier, Paradise sunset
summary: South over Blewett Pass and Chinook Pass, then an afternoon at Paradise ending with sunset at Reflection Lakes.

segments.name: Segment 1 — Leavenworth to Chinook Pass via Blewett Pass
segments.blurb: US-97 over Blewett Pass, then west on SR-410 toward the park.

stops.name: Blewett Pass
stops.note: US-97 summit between the Wenatchee and Yakima valleys.

stops.name: Naches
stops.note: Small town where SR-410 branches off toward Chinook Pass.

stops.name: Chinook Pass Entrance Arch
stops.note: Log entrance arch marking the park boundary at the summit.

expect.arrive: Two mountain passes back to back on two-lane highway; Blewett Pass and the Chinook Pass entrance arch are quick roadside pull-offs, not destinations.
expect.parking: Gravel shoulders only at both summits, room for a handful of cars, never busy.

paths.do: Photo stop at the entrance arch only, no detours.
Coffee or gas stop in Naches before the climb to the pass.

segments.seasonal: This whole segment depends on SR-410 over Chinook Pass being open. WSDOT's typical closing date is late October — Oct 24, 2025; Oct 31, 2024 (an early storm closure); Nov 10, 2023 — so Oct 3 is normally well clear, but 2024's closure shows an early cold snap can force it shut with little notice. Check wsdot.wa.gov/travel/roads-bridges/mountain-pass-closure-and-opening-dates the morning of departure; there is no good detour if it's closed (the alternative is back through Yakima and up I-5, adding hours).

segments.name: Segment 2 — Tipsoo Lake and Chinook Pass
segments.blurb: Short stop at the alpine lake; SR-410 can close for winter by late October.

stops.name: Tipsoo Lake
stops.note: Short loop trail; Rainier reflected in the lake when calm.

stops.name: Naches Peak Loop Trail
stops.note: 3.2-mile loop from the pass, optional if time allows.

stops.name: Cayuse Pass
stops.note: Junction where SR-410 meets SR-123 heading south into the park.

expect.arrive: Small alpine lake right off the highway at the pass; Rainier reflects in it on still mornings but the mountain is frequently clouded over within minutes since it makes its own weather.
expect.parking: Small paved lot at the pass, plus a bit of shoulder; rarely full this late in the season on a weekday.

paths.do: Walk the easy path around Tipsoo Lake itself.
Short drive to the Cayuse Pass junction for a photo, no walking.
Full loop trail from the pass with real elevation gain but no scrambling.

segments.seasonal: SR-410/Chinook Pass and SR-123/Cayuse Pass close together — see d09s1 for the closure risk. No official round-trip distance for the short walk around Tipsoo Lake itself was found on nps.gov; the NPS page (nps.gov/mora/planyourvisit/day-hiking-at-mount-rainier.htm) only lists the connecting Naches Peak Loop Trail at 3.4 mi / 2h, so the lake-loop trail object is omitted rather than estimated.

segments.name: Segment 3 — Paradise, Myrtle Falls, Nisqually Vista
segments.blurb: The two short, well-known trails from the Paradise parking lot.

stops.name: Henry M. Jackson Visitor Center
stops.q: Henry M Jackson Visitor Center Paradise
stops.note: Starting point for the Paradise trails.

stops.name: Myrtle Falls
stops.note: 0.8-mile round trip on the Skyline Trail; the park's most photographed falls.

trail.from: Paradise upper parking lot / Jackson Visitor Center

stops.name: Nisqually Vista Trail
stops.note: 1.2-mile loop over Nisqually Glacier and valley views.

trail.from: Paradise lower parking lot, Nisqually Vista trailhead

stops.name: Skyline Trail
stops.note: Longer option climbing above Myrtle Falls toward Panorama Point.

trail.from: Paradise upper parking lot, next to the visitor center
trail.grade: strenuous — the full loop is out of scope for this trip; if walking any of it, turn around at or before the Golden Gate Trail junction (about 2 mi in, near Panorama Point) rather than completing the loop
trail.caveat: The full loop. The Golden Gate Trail cuts it shorter, but NPS publishes no figure for that

expect.arrive: Wide subalpine meadow below the summit; the mountain is visible maybe half the time even in good weather and is frequently clouded over for hours at a stretch — plan the visit assuming you might not see it.
expect.parking: Two lots (upper near the visitor center, lower near the Nisqually Vista trailhead) that together hold a few hundred cars; they fill by mid-to-late morning on clear fall weekends, easier on a Saturday afternoon arrival at this time of year.

paths.do: Paved path from the visitor center up to the falls overlook and back.
Both easy, mostly flat/paved trails, no real climbing, from two different lots.
Continue past Myrtle Falls onto the Skyline Trail toward Panorama Point via the Golden Gate cutoff, a real climb but no scrambling — only worth it if the mountain is out and legs are willing.
paths.cost: 2-2.5h round trip to Golden Gate junction and back

alt: Henry M Jackson Visitor Center Paradise
segments.seasonal: No timed-entry reservation is needed anywhere in the park in 2026 — NPS cancelled the system this year and is managing crowding through parking only (nps.gov/mora/planyourvisit/timed-entry-reservations.htm). The Jackson Visitor Center moves to winter hours on October 14 (10am-5pm, weekends/holidays only through year-end) per NPS-sourced reporting, so on October 3 it should still be on its daily fall schedule — but confirm hours close to the date since the exact 2026 daily-to-winter cutover date wasn't independently verified beyond that secondary source.

segments.name: Segment 4 — Sunset at Reflection Lakes
segments.blurb: Short drive from Paradise for the classic mountain-in-lake sunset shot.

map.center: Reflection Lakes, Mount Rainier National Park

stops.name: Reflection Lakes
stops.note: Pull-off on Stevens Canyon Road, a few minutes from Paradise.

trail.from: Reflection Lakes pull-off, Stevens Canyon Road
trail.grade: moderate — a flat shoreline-only stroll is possible but has no official separate distance
trail.caveat: That is the full Lakes Trail to Faraway Rock. The shoreline by the car is a few minutes

stops.name: Louise Lake
stops.note: Smaller lake just past Reflection Lakes, fewer crowds.

stops.name: Narada Falls
stops.note: 168-foot falls on the way back toward Paradise.

expect.arrive: A short pull-off on Stevens Canyon Road a few minutes from Paradise; this is the classic mountain-in-lake shot but it only works if the water is glassy and the summit is actually visible, neither guaranteed.
expect.parking: Small roadside lot plus turnouts along the road; fills right at sunset in good weather, arrive 30-45 min early to get a spot.

paths.do: Park at the main pull-off, walk to the water's edge, no trail.
Short drive further along Stevens Canyon Road and back toward Paradise.

paths.opt: Walk part of the Lakes Trail shoreline
paths.do: Follow the trail along the lake edge partway without committing to the full loop up to Faraway Rock.

segments.seasonal: nps.gov/places/reflection-lakes.htm gives only the roughly 3-mile Lakes Trail loop to Faraway Rock, with no NPS time estimate and no separate official number for a shoreline-only walk — the trail object above reflects that gap rather than an estimate for the shorter stroll.
